title: Affine-open base case for perfect Hom continuity
statement: Let $I$ be a preordered set, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram, $c$ a cocone, $i\in I$, and $s:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Assume the scheme derived categories of [def-pc-derived-category] exist. In addition, suppose $I$ is directed, $c$ is colimiting, and $s$ is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$, the condition $\mathcal C(U)$ of [def-pc-perfect-hom-continuity-on] holds.

proof.text: Every open-immersion presentation Y of U is affine. Perfect complexes have quasi-coherent cohomology. Use the affine bounded-projective criterion and the affine derived equivalence to represent both by bounded finite-projective complexes of modules over the coordinate ring of Y.

The base changes of Y have rings B_i tensor over R_i with R_j and c.pt; tensor extension preserves colimits. Since the model complexes have flat terms, affine derived pullback is ordinary scalar extension. Its natural tilde comparison identifies the Hom transport with the canonical conjugated maps, using counit-pinned composition coherence.

Apply affine_perfect_hom_colimit to the identified module-derived Hom diagram. A common upper bound proves that every tail is cofinal, giving a representative above each j0. Injectivity and the filtered-set equality criterion give equality at some later k, and composition coherence propagates equality for all l at least k.
